_about: The evaluator contract: a metric card is the JSON a problem's evaluator writes for one named system on one split (runs/eval/<name>/<split>[_<subset>].json for lcr). Everything downstream (decide.py, experiment.py, metrics.py, reports) reads cards, never numbers typed by hand. Any problem plugs in by writing cards of this shape: an ML model evaluated on a validation split, or a code system benchmarked by a script (then 'n' is the number of benchmark runs or test cases and 'seeds' are repeats). Checked by autoresearch/tools/card.py check. Plain JSON, no JSON-Schema library: 'required' / 'types' / 'fields' as in experiment.schema.json.

fields.name: the registry name of the system evaluated (models/registry.json for lcr; any stable name for another problem)
fields.split: the data split or benchmark set the numbers come from (val | test | confirm | <benchmark name>); the holdout split (project.json holdout_split, default test) needs a logged id
fields.subset: a named subset of the split (val250) or empty
fields.fresh: true when the numbers were computed without the evaluator's cache
fields.frames: the denominator: number of frames (lcr) - or
fields.n: the denominator: number of samples / benchmark runs / test cases (generic name; a card has frames or n)
fields.metrics: {metric name: number}; the headline metrics of the problem must be present (PROBLEM.md); lower-is-better metrics are known by the experiment file's direction, else by name (project.json lower_is_better, plus the generic ms names of decide.py LOWER)
fields.commit: the code commit the numbers were made with ('+dirty' when tracked files differed, '+?' when unknown)
fields.registry: the registry entry used (checkpoint, config, standard settings) - lcr
fields.overrides: settings changed for this card (recorded, so a card is never silently non-standard)
fields.info: evaluator details: cache file, assembly settings, ms per frame, seconds for the metrics
fields.compare: {name, metrics, paired: {metric: {diff, lo, hi}}}: the paired bootstrap against another name on the same samples (evaluate.py --compare); decide.py uses lo / hi as the interval
fields.settings: generic: the settings of the evaluation for a non-lcr problem (benchmark version, hardware)

bare_metrics: a flat {metric: number} dict without 'metrics' is accepted by decide.py as a bare card (loop-18 result files) but fails `card.py check`: new evaluators write full cards
